title: Finite quotient pullback normalization on a good complex
statement: Fix l,E,Operations o, RealizationModel model, an arbitrary scheme morphism f:X→Y, a flat-term K-flat good completed-coefficient cochain complex P on Y, and n≥0. Write K=Q(P), ρ_W for the reductionEvaluation isomorphism, k for the specified pullbackTensorDerivedEvaluation and h=model.reductionPull(f). Then finiteScalarPullback(f,n) inverse at K followed by ρ_X inverse at ringedPull(f)(K) equals finiteDerivedPullback(f) of ρ_Y inverse at K, followed by k inverse at reduction(K), followed by finite evaluation of h inverse at K. The finiteScalarPullback is the canonical specified isomorphism of [def-sf-integral-finite-pullback-coordinates]. No reconstruction counit or derived proper direct image is involved.

proof.text: For any additive adjunction with exact left adjoint, derive its Hom transpose equation on homotopy representatives from derivedη_fac_app and naturality of the right-derived unit. Apply normalizedAdjunction_uniqueness and localization extensionality to show that deriving the ordinary leftAdjointUniq comparison equals leftAdjointUniq of the derived adjunctions and the derived right comparison. Specialize to finiteDirectImage_eq and the two geometric module adjunctions. This identifies finiteRingPullbackIso with mapDerivedCategoryNatIso(finitePullbackIso).

Expand the two specified scalar/pullback presentation isomorphisms. Substitute the finite pullback identification of Step 1, and use naturality to move finiteReductionIso(Y,n) across the finite geometric pullback comparison. Thus finiteScalarPullback equals the already specified integralFiniteScalarPull; no definition or adjunction is changed.

Apply integralReductionPullFiniteSquare to K=Q(P). Package the evaluated reductionPull, pullbackTensorDerivedEvaluation, and finite pullback of reductionEvaluation as a composite isomorphism; its forward arrow equals reductionEvaluation(X,n) followed by integralFiniteScalarPull. Equality of isomorphisms gives equality of their inverses. Expand the inverses in reverse order, use mapIso_inv, substitute Step 2 and reassociate. This is exactly the stated equation, with no use of the good-complex property beyond its supplied object.

theorem integralFinitePullback_onGood (o : Operations l E)
    (model : RealizationModel l E o) {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (P : (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E Y).FullSubcategory) (n : ℕ) :
    (finiteScalarPullback l E f n).inv.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P.obj) ≫
        ((calculus l E X).reductionEvaluation n).inv.app
          ((ringedPull l E f).obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P.obj)) =
      (finiteDerivedPullback l E n f).map
          (((calculus l E Y).reductionEvaluation n).inv.app
            (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P.obj)) ≫
        (pullbackTensorDerivedEvaluation l E f n).inv.app
          ((calculus l E Y).reduction.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P.obj)) ≫
        (coefficientSequenceDerivedEvaluation l E X n).map
          ((model.reductionPull f).inv.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P.obj))
